name: ffuf
what: A fast web fuzzer written in Go. It discovers hidden paths, virtual hosts and parameters by injecting a wordlist into marked parts of an HTTP request and filtering responses by status, size or regex.
when: During authorized web app tests when you need content discovery beyond what a spider sees, or when validating that staging sites do not expose leftover admin paths.
example: Directory discovery against an approved staging host: `ffuf -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/common.txt -u https://staging.contoso.com/FUZZ -mc 200,204,301,302,403`.
Tune with `-rate`, `-fc`/`-fs` filters and a recursion depth that matches the rules of engagement.
Export results (`-o findings.json -of json`) and verify each hit manually before reporting.
pitfalls: Aggressive wordlists and threads can overwhelm fragile apps or WAFs; start slow on production-like systems.
Matching only on HTTP 200 misses many interesting responses; learn the app's baseline sizes first.
Never fuzz authentication or payment flows without explicit approval and test accounts.
